original_question: If lambda_1, ..., lambda_n are linearly independent over Q and e^{lambda_1}, ..., e^{lambda_n} are algebraic, must lambda_1, ..., lambda_n be algebraically independent over Q?
target_in_paper: Conjecture 3.3 in §3.1, Algebraic Independence of Logarithms of Algebraic Numbers. It is introduced there as the most important special case of Schanuel’s Conjecture. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0312440))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the exact official conjecture almost verbatim: the hypothesis that λ1, ..., λn are Q-linearly independent, the assumption that e^{λ1}, ..., e^{λn} are algebraic, and the conclusion that λ1, ..., λn should be algebraically independent over Q. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0312440))
missing_details: The paper states explicitly that λ1, ..., λn are complex numbers; that ambient domain is omitted in the draft. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0312440))

To make the question fully stand-alone, e^{λ1}, ..., e^{λn} should be identified as algebraic numbers, i.e. elements of the field of algebraic numbers inside C. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0312440))
The quantifier on n is implicit in the draft but explicit in a self-contained formulation: the conjecture is for arbitrary n ≥ 1. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0312440))
refined_question: Conjecture 3.3 (§3.1): Let n ≥ 1 and let λ1, ..., λn ∈ C be Q-linearly independent. If e^{λ1}, ..., e^{λn} are algebraic numbers, must λ1, ..., λn be algebraically independent over Q? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0312440))
equivalent_formulation: Equivalent reformulation due to D. Roy: if L denotes the set of complex numbers λ such that e^λ is algebraic, then for any algebraic subvariety V of C^n defined over the field of algebraic numbers, the set V ∩ L^n is the union of the sets E ∩ L^n, where E ranges over the vector subspaces of C^n contained in V. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0312440))
justification: The draft is targeting exactly Conjecture 3.3 in §3.1, not a broader neighboring problem. Waldschmidt first states Schanuel’s Conjecture as Conjecture 3.1 and then immediately singles out Conjecture 3.3 as its most important special case. The wording of your draft matches Conjecture 3.3 essentially exactly; the only paper-critical additions needed for a fully stand-alone version are the ambient domain λi ∈ C, the interpretation of e^{λi} as algebraic numbers, and the explicit quantifier n ≥ 1. The Roy statement is included as the single alternate formulation because the paper itself presents it as a reformulation of Conjecture 3.3. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0312440))
